title: Autoscale inertia soak profiling: steady-state + microburst regression detection
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Implement a long-running soak and targeted microburst harness that profiles autoscaler inertia and p95 latency regressions for Dedicated capacity. The harness should exercise steady-state throughput with periodic short-duration spikes to validate autoscaler decision timing, cooldown behavior, and fallback triggers. Capture token/sec, per-request p95, model-variant fallbacks, KV cache hit/miss heatmap, GPU utilization, kernel selection shifts, and autoscaler actions (scale_up/scale_down) with timestamps. The goal is to detect subtle regressions (>=10% p95 regression) with high sensitivity while keeping false positives below 5%.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end harness able to run unattended for 72 hours against a Dedicated pool and produce a single TSV/CSV with time-series of tokens_sec, p95_ms, p50_ms, kv_cache_hit_rate, gbench_gpu_util, model_variant, autoscale_event_type, autoscale_reason
Regression detector flags a 10% increase in rolling 15-minute p95 within 30 minutes of occurrence with >=90% sensitivity in synthetic validation runs
False positive alert rate <= 5% measured over 20 synthetic no-regression runs
Microburst profile: 2-minute spike to 200% nominal tokens/sec should trigger either warm-burst autoscale or graceful degradation path; harness verifies recovery window <= 10 minutes from spike end
Soak profile: maintain 60% average pool utilization for 72 hours without unmet request queue growth (> 1s queue depth sustained)
Telemetry capture includes KV cache cold vs warm scenario comparison and shows p95 delta with cache misses
Artifact: reproducible runbook and a Grafana dashboard template for p95 drift, token/sec, and autoscaler events
runbook_steps: 1) Provision a dedicated test pool (tag: harness-autoscale-inertia) with 8x of the production pod size
2) Load generator config: steady-state target = 60% of pool nominal tokens/sec, inject microbursts every 4 hours: 2-minute ramp to 200% tokens/sec, 30s ramp-down
3) Two KV cache modes: cold-start (clear cache before run) and warm-start (preload common prefixes) — run both back-to-back
4) Start telemetry ingestion: per-request traces, model_variant, kernel_version, gpu metrics, and autoscaler logs to centralized trace store
5) Run harness for 72 hours; monitor p95 control chart and EWMA alerts; record all autoscaler events
6) On alert, capture flamegraph of inference runtime for the 10-minute window surrounding alert
7) Produce CSV/TSV artifact and push to /artifacts/perf/harness/ENG-91900 with summary markdown
test_design_notes: We will use a hybrid generator that can target both tokens/sec and request/sec simultaneously to simulate bursty user patterns (long prompts vs many short prompts).

Regression detector: primary signal will be a rolling 15-minute p95 baseline with EWMA smoothing and a Student t-based drift test. Secondary signal: sudden increase in autoscaler churn or sustained queue depth growth.
Control for noise: compare against a control pool shadowed with identical config but not receiving bursts to reduce false positives due to infra noise.
KV cache: instrument prefix distribution and TTL churn; include a mode where we intentionally flush cache mid-soak to measure cold restore cost.
Autoscaler observation: capture decision latency (time from threshold breach to scale event) and compare to configured cooldown windows; test both conservative and aggressive scaler policies.
Define minimal repro: if a regression is detected, the harness must be able to replay the exact traffic file for 30 minutes to reproduce the p95 spike locally.
observed_risks_and_mitigations: Risk: autoscaler oscillation during repeated microbursts could create noise and mask regressions. Mitigation: include a shadow control pool and tune burst cadence to allow stabilization windows.
Risk: telemetry cardinality (kernel_version + model_variant) may explode. Mitigation: sample traces at 1% and aggregate kernel/model tags into buckets for dashboarding.
Risk: long soak runs consume quota and could affect other teams. Mitigation: schedule runs during a reserved test window and tag resources to prevent accidental reuse.
Risk: false positives from GC pauses or infra maintenance. Mitigation: correlate cloud-host maintenance events and exclude those windows from regression scoring.
